title: Opossums Aren't Faking It When They Play Dead
subject: virginia opossum

scenes.text: When an opossum plays dead, it isn't acting.
It's an involuntary reaction to extreme stress. The opossum goes limp, its heart and breathing slow, and its body temperature falls.
It can last for hours. Wildlife experts say to wait at least four hours before deciding one has really died.
The same animal also resists snake venom, especially from rattlesnakes and other pit vipers.
A protein in its blood neutralizes venom toxins, and scientists are studying it for human snakebite care.
So it isn't playing dead. It's fainting.
